tasks.gr9-reading-cartoons-visual-texts-t1: Topic: Reading cartoons and visual texts (Grade 9 English Home Language, Term 1). Cover frames, speech and thought bubbles, captions, reading order, exaggeration, symbols (dove, scales), caricature, layout and where the eye goes first, tone, and stating the message (who or what is criticised and what the cartoonist wants). Describe any cartoon in words; no copied artwork. Ask Grade 9 questions.
tasks.gr9-summary-writing-t2: Topic: Summary writing (Grade 9 English Home Language, Term 2). Cover what a summary keeps and leaves out, finding the main point of a paragraph, key words, own words, replacing long phrases with short ones (in order to to to, due to the fact that to because), word-limit arithmetic (a limit of one third: 240 words gives 80; 5 points about 16 words each; 11 words cut to 6 saves 5) and checking the count. Use original passages. No marks. Ask Grade 9 questions.
tasks.gr9-prose-plot-setting-conflict-t3: Topic: Prose, plot, setting and conflict (Grade 9 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover the five plot stages (exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution), setting (place, time, mood), and conflict (person against person, self, nature, society), using original short passages only and no quoted published story. No marks. Ask Grade 9 questions.
tasks.gr9-prose-character-narrator-theme-t3: Topic: Prose, character, narrator and theme (Grade 9 English Home Language, Term 3). Cover direct and indirect characterisation, round and flat characters, first-person, third-person and omniscient narrators, topic versus theme and how to find the theme, using original short passages only and no quoted published story. No marks. Ask Grade 9 questions.
tasks.gr9-prose-contextual-questions-t4: Topic: Answering contextual questions on prose (Grade 9 English Home Language, Term 4). Cover reading the whole extract first, reading the question twice, command words (state, quote, explain, describe), short quotations as evidence, inference, and the point, evidence, explanation pattern; more marks mean more points but no real mark allocations. Use original extracts only. Ask Grade 9 questions.
